Profile Summary

“I believe great design begins with understanding people and their needs.”

I’m Kay, a UX Designer and Researcher with an extensive background in the travel industry and a Master’s in Human-Computer Interaction and UX Design from Drexel University.

Currently a UX Design Intern at Resilience Inc., I combine research, creativity, and empathy to design intuitive, accessible, and meaningful digital experiences. I’m excited to bring my skills and perspective to a full-time UX role.

The Story Behind the Designer

Four chapters. One evolving journey.

Chapter One · The Beginning

Where I Started

For many years, I worked in the travel industry, helping travelers navigate complicated booking platforms and make confident decisions. I often found myself simplifying information and making overwhelming processes easier to understand. These experiences sparked my curiosity: What if technology was designed to make things simpler from the start? Looking back, my UX journey began long before I knew what UX was, rooted in a passion for understanding people, solving problems, and creating better experiences.

Chapter Two

My UX Journey

While I enjoyed helping people navigate their experiences, I wanted to do more than work around the challenges they encountered, and to help solve them. As technology became a bigger part of everyday life, I grew curious about the decisions behind digital products and how thoughtful design could make them more intuitive, accessible, and enjoyable. That curiosity led me to a Master’s program in Human-Computer Interaction and UX Design at Drexel University, where I began turning my experience helping travelers into a foundation for human-centered design.

Three projects shaped my journey: ZenRoute, a calmer and more accessible way to plan travel; Bargain Beacon, an exploration of in-store shopping assistance; and Kitchen Connect, a voice-based cooking concept. Each one challenged me to ask better questions and approach problems from the user’s perspective. Along the way, I discovered that UX brings together what I’ve always valued: curiosity, creativity, empathy, and meaningful problem-solving.

Chapter Three

What I’ve Learned

Simplicity earns attention, both in interfaces and in portfolios. I’ve learned to let research guide my decisions, tell meaningful stories through design, and embrace creativity along the way. While working on ZenRoute, I discovered that more features don’t always mean better experiences. Usability testing showed that guided assistance improved the experience, while excessive alerts increased cognitive load. This reinforced an important lesson: thoughtful design is about simplifying decisions, not creating more of them. Above all, I’ve learned to stay curious, listen to users, and remain open to rethinking my approach.

Chapter Four

What’s Next

I’m currently a UX Design Intern at Resilience Inc., gaining hands-on experience in human-centered design, creative problem-solving, and collaboration. I’m excited to join a team where research and design come together to create meaningful digital experiences. I look forward to expanding my skills in UX research, accessibility, design systems, and emerging technologies like AI, while exploring opportunities to support nonprofits through volunteer design projects. For me, growth means staying curious, embracing new challenges, and always keeping people at the heart of design.
